source_caption:
𝐒𝐮𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐛𝐚𝐝 (𝟐𝟎𝟎𝟕) has one of the most unique origin stories in modern comedy. What makes the movie special is that it isn’t just inspired by teenage life but was literally written by two teenagers.⁣
⁣
Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg began writing the script in the mid-1990s when they were just 13 years old, growing up in Vancouver, Canada. Much like the film itself, they were awkward high school friends obsessed with girls, parties, and trying to fit in before graduation. Instead of inventing outrageous situations, they simply wrote about the conversations they were actually having in real life. In fact, the two main characters, Seth and Evan, are named after the writers themselves.⁣
⁣
The script spent nearly a decade in development. As Rogen’s acting career began to take off with projects like Freaks and Geeks and The 40-Year-Old Virgin, producer Judd Apatow became interested in bringing the screenplay to life. By then, however, Rogen was already too old to play the teenage version of himself. Instead, Jonah Hill was cast as Seth, while Michael Cera perfectly captured Evan’s shy and anxious personality.

source_details.title: Superbad
source_details.synopsis: Superbad is a 2007 American coming-of-age teen buddy comedy film directed by Greg Mottola, written by Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg, and produced by Judd Apatow. It stars Jonah Hill and Michael Cera as Seth and Evan, two teenagers about to graduate from high school. Before graduating, the boys want to party and lose their virginity, but their plan proves harder than expected. Christopher Mintz-Plasse (in his film debut), Rogen, Bill Hader, Martha MacIsaac, and Emma Stone (in her film debut) provide supporting roles. Rogen and Goldberg wrote the script during their teenage years. It is loosely based on their experience in Grade 12 at Point Grey Secondary School in Vancouver during the 1990s. T
